core.title: Ask the user for missing acceptance context; never infer or suggest it
core.given: You are extracting an acceptance and some context (e.g. which bounded slice of the product it belongs to) is missing from what the user has stated.
core.when: You need to obtain or fill in that missing context.
core.then: Obtain the missing context by asking the user directly — do not infer it and do not offer suggestions.
prefer: Pure conversational extraction: ask the user directly about the gap in the acceptance's context.
Wait for the user's answer before writing the context into the acceptance.
avoid: Guessing (inferring) missing acceptance context from surrounding material and writing it in.
Offering suggestions or pre-filled candidate answers instead of asking directly.
core.why: No inference is the policy of asking rather than guessing missing acceptance context; direct extraction supplies the context the abstract acceptance fields require and keeps the acceptance complete and faithful to the user's intent.
evidence: Every piece of acceptance context that was not in the user's original request traces to a direct question asked of the user and the user's answer.
The conversation contains no inferred values or suggestion lists presented in place of a direct question.
verification: No mechanical detector covers this rule: whether any piece of acceptance context is missing from the user's request or prior answers can only be judged by an LLM today.
Acceptance context filled without a user-sourced answer is not observable today; detecting it would need a new observer that traces the conversation to the drafted artifact.

Compliance is the generic policy check 'asking rather than guessing', established conversationally against the evidence items: context traces to direct questions and answers, and no inferred values or suggestion lists appear in place of a direct question.

Activation on file kinds goes through the plan_artifact role: the concrete planner artifact kinds that trigger the rule are the structure profile's roles.plan_artifact.kinds, not a list owned by the rule.

values: acceptance context missing from what the user supplied

fires: Drafting an acceptance and the user has not said which bounded slice of the product it belongs to.
Any acceptance context needed while extracting the acceptance is absent from the user's request or prior answers.
doesNotFire: All acceptance context being used was explicitly stated by the user.
Work that is not acceptance extraction (e.g. coding against an already-complete acceptance).

neutralityNotes: This planner-conversation rule is almost entirely stack-neutral: the obligation depends on no repository structure, tooling or enforcement machinery. The one profile datum it needs is the set of concrete planner artifact kinds for its file_kind activation, supplied as roles.plan_artifact.kinds (acceptance, plan, wagon in the reference realization), so instantiating the core with the realization's profile restores the original file-kind activation exactly; the 'wagon' kind is profile data, not a realization-only exception. Residual realization-specific content, all kept in bun.json as the worked reference: the rule-specific task terms 'wagon' and 'WMBT'; the finding id 'acceptance_context_missing'; the canonical wagon_inference prompt and its example question; the no_inference term id; and the 'wagon' wording of the concrete examples in given and prefer[0] (the core generalizes it to 'bounded slice of the product', including in activation.fires[0], which has no item id of its own). The observability notes of the activation facts (LLM-judged missingness; a would-be conversation-to-artifact trace observer) are carried as generic scope statements in core.verification.
